newsitem.title: UK: W.Cook sets buyout to thwart Triplex.
newsitem.headline: W.Cook sets buyout to thwart Triplex.

text.p: The executive chairman of British steel castings specialist William Cook Plc launched an 80 milllion pound ($131 million), venture capital-backed buyout bid for the company on Thursday in an attempt to thwart hostile bidder Triplex Lloyd Plc.

Steel Castings Investments is the brainchild of Andrew Cook, who has battled hard to fight off Triplex's attentions. It said its bid would offer William Cook shareholders 425 pence cash per unit, compared with a full cash alternative of 383.4 pence per share in Triplex Lloyd's latest bid.
W.Cook sets buyout to thwart Triplex =2

Steel Castings Investments, backed by venture capitalists Electra Fleming, includes the existing top management of William Cook, and Andrew Cook has already agreed to sell it his interest in 860,846 shares, representing 4.6 percent of William Cook's share capital.

Lawrence Banks, chairman of the investment vehicle, said in a statement, "This cash offer of 425 pence per share offers good value to shareholders and is in the best interests of the company, its customers and employees.

When Triplex raised its bid earlier this week it said its share-based offer was worth 400.7 pence per William Cook share and valued the group at 74.8 million pounds. However, its own share price has since fallen, making this part of the bid worth slightly less. William Cook's shares, which were suspended earlier in the day pending an announcement, resumed trade at 415 pence, up from their Wednesday close of 380 pence, and later climbed to 420 pence.
